title: Awarapan 2 Eyes ₹11-16 Crore Opening in Independence Day Clash With Batwara 1947
excerpt: Emraan Hashmi's sequel to the 2007 cult classic is projected to open at double the original's lifetime collection, but underwhelming music has tempered early estimates.
body:
• Awarapan 2 is projected to open at ₹11-16 crore net on August 14, clashing with Sunny Deol's Batwara 1947 on Independence Day weekend
  • The sequel could earn double the original 2007 film's ₹7.75 crore lifetime collection on opening day alone
  • Disha Patani is expected to register her 6th highest opener, falling short of her top 5 due to Welcome To The Jungle's ₹19.4 crore

Awarapan 2, the long-awaited sequel to the 2007 cult classic starring Emraan Hashmi and Disha Patani, is tracking for a double-digit opening when it hits theatres on August 14, 2026. The Vishesh Films production, directed by Nitin Kakkar, faces a direct clash with Sunny Deol's partition drama Batwara 1947 on what promises to be a fiercely competitive Independence Day weekend.

Opening Day Projections Show Wide Range

Trade estimates for Awarapan 2's opening day have fluctuated significantly in the weeks leading up to release. Early projections from Koimoi pegged the film at ₹25 crore net, which would have made it roughly three times the original's entire ₹7.75 crore lifetime haul on day one alone. Pinkvilla's forecast settled at ₹12-17 crore, while Sacnilk projected around ₹15 crore.

However, more recent estimates have tempered expectations. The underwhelming reception of the film's initial songs — traditionally a make-or-break factor for Vishesh Films productions — has pulled projections down to the ₹11-16 crore range. The original Awarapan's Pritam-composed soundtrack was central to its cult status, and trade analysts note that Awarapan 2's music hasn't generated the same viral momentum.

"The people who made the first film a cult object mostly did so at home, years after it left cinemas."

— Boxoffy analysis

Independence Day Clash With Batwara 1947

The August 14 release date sets up a rematch of sorts. In June 2007, Sunny Deol's Apne opened against the original Awarapan on the same Friday, with Sunny winning that round comfortably — ₹69.28 crore against ₹12 crore. Nineteen years later, both camps are back on the same date.

Batwara 1947, formerly titled Lahore 1947, is directed by Rajkumar Santoshi and produced by Aamir Khan Productions. The partition drama stars Sunny Deol, Preity Zinta, Karan Deol, and Shabana Azmi. Despite the heavyweight cast and subject-to-date alignment with Independence Day, Batwara 1947 is tracking lower at ₹4-7 crore for its opening day, with Awarapan 2 expected to win the footfall battle.

Both films stand to benefit from the long weekend, with Independence Day falling on a Saturday this year, giving audiences an extended window to catch both releases.

Where Disha Patani Stands Among Her Top Openers

For Disha Patani, Awarapan 2 represents a chance to add another solid opener to her filmography, though her top 5 appears out of reach. Her biggest opening remains Bharat at ₹42.30 crore, followed by Baaghi 2 (₹25.10 crore), Kalki 2898 AD Hindi (₹22.5 crore), MS Dhoni (₹21.30 crore), and Welcome To The Jungle (₹19.4 crore).

At the projected ₹11-16 crore range, Awarapan 2 would slot in as her 6th highest opener, comfortably ahead of Ek Villain Returns (₹7.05 crore) and Malang (₹6.71 crore) but unable to breach the ₹19.4 crore barrier set by Welcome To The Jungle.

Nostalgia Factor Carries the Campaign

The original Awarapan earned just ₹7.75 crore in its entire theatrical run in 2007 but built a devoted following through television reruns and streaming over nearly two decades. Mohit Suri's direction and Pritam's soundtrack — particularly tracks like "Toh Phir Aao" — became staples of the romantic drama genre.

The sequel leans heavily into this nostalgia. Emraan Hashmi returns as Shivam Pandit in what is written as a direct continuation rather than a reboot, with Shabana Azmi joining the cast. For Emraan, who has struggled at the box office in recent years, a ₹15 crore-plus opening could register as his 3rd biggest ever in India.

What's Next

The final promotional push, including the recreation of "Toh Phir Aao" and the theatrical trailer, could still shift projections upward. Advance booking numbers, which open in the coming days, will provide a clearer picture. For diaspora audiences who grew up with the original's music on repeat, the sequel represents one of the more emotionally charged Bollywood releases of the year.
